ground_truth_core_content:
Introduction:
**0:** The generated introduction covers the previous-lessons recap, the static-knowledge/closed-book-exam framing, fine-tuning's shortfalls, the RAG-as-open-book-exam solution, the Context Engineering tie-in, the Lesson-10 memory/long-term-store contrast, and the lesson roadmap. However, as in every replicate of this lesson graded so far, the expected section's entire context-window paragraph -- context as working memory, its finite/costly nature, 'lost in the middle', and 'selection beats stuffing' -- is completely absent. The expected section also previews exposing the knowledge base as a tool wired into the ReAct loop to define Agentic RAG; the generated introduction defers this entirely to the dedicated Agentic RAG section later in the article.

The RAG System: Core Components:
**1:** Both sections cover the same three pillars -- Retrieval (vector embeddings, semantic search), Augmentation (formatting retrieved text into the prompt), and Generation (LLM synthesizes a grounded answer) -- with matching substance. The generated section's early mention of BM25 within the Retrieval pillar is an accepted complementary addition that does not displace any expected idea.

The RAG Pipeline: Ingestion and Retrieval:
**1:** Both phases (Offline Ingestion: load/split/embed/store; Online Retrieval: query/embed/search/generate, including the Lesson 4 structured-outputs callback) are present with matching substance and tool names. The expected section's aside about long-context embedding models and its second, duplicate static image are absent, but the guideline explicitly instructs omitting exactly that content, so this is not treated as a missing substantive idea here.

Advanced RAG Techniques:
**0:** This is one of the more complete treatments of this section seen across the replicates graded so far: Hybrid Search and Re-ranking (with the connect-my-account example) match the expected section, HyDE includes its specific drafted-answer example, Advanced Chunking covers all three named techniques (semantic, layout-aware, context-enriched), and GraphRAG adds a well-anchored, exploration-sourced elaboration on Implicit Relationship Hallucination (see depth_enhancement below). The sole gap is the expected section's Metadata Filtering subsection (temporal filters, bitemporal effective_date/indexed_at logic), which has no counterpart anywhere in the generated section. Per the standing ruling, a missing Metadata Filtering subsection guarantees this score regardless of how complete the rest of the section is.

Agentic RAG:
**1:** The ReAct tie-in, the standard-vs-agentic distinction, all four expected capabilities (iterative refinement, choosing a knowledge source, fusing with other tools, and updating the knowledge base as a Lesson 10 preview), and the EU-data-retention thought-process example are all present with matching substance. This is the most complete capability coverage for this section seen across the replicates graded so far.

Conclusion:
**1:** Both sections summarize RAG's role in solving the LLM knowledge problem, explicitly state that advanced techniques matter for production-grade quality, restate the future-is-agentic framing, cover all three core benefits (hallucinations, proprietary-data customization, verifiable trust), position RAG as a foundational competency within Context Engineering, and transition to Lesson 10 (Memory) plus later course topics (evaluation, monitoring). This is a fully complete match with no gaps.

References:
**1:** Both sections contain a numbered list of references serving the same bibliographic purpose.
